Package com.macstab.chaos.jvm.core

@NullMarked package com.macstab.chaos.jvm.core
The chaos runtime: scenario registry, dispatch, effects and stressors.

Every type is non-null unless annotated @Nullable.

  • Class
    Description
    AgentHookThread
    A thread of the agent that the JDK starts, not the agent: a shutdown hook.
    AgentLog
    The agent's java.util.logging lines.
    AgentThreads
    Starts and stops the agent's own threads (stressor and expiry threads), so no scenario is ever evaluated for them (L3): each body runs, and each thread is started and stopped, with the dispatch depth raised.
    ChaosDispatcher
    The hot-path dispatch of the chaos runtime: the entry points the instrumentation layer calls through the bootstrap bridge (see BootstrapDispatcher), one class per domain — ThreadDispatch, ExecutorDispatch, MethodDispatch, ClockDispatch, RuntimeDispatch, NetworkDispatch, DnsDispatch, FileDispatch, ProcessDispatch, ClientDispatch — over one shared DispatchEngine.
    ChaosRuntime
    Thin facade that composes ChaosControlPlaneImpl and ChaosDispatcher.
    ClientDispatch
    Dispatch of client-library calls: HTTP clients, JDBC and the messaging, RPC, cache and cloud clients.
    ClockDispatch
    Clock skew of the JVM clock reads: System call sites, java.time, the system Clock and java.util.Date.
    DefaultChaosActivationHandle
    Default implementation of ChaosActivationHandle.
    DnsDispatch
    Dispatch of DNS lookups: forward resolution, the answer returned, and reverse lookups.
    ExecutorDispatch
    Dispatch of executor, scheduler, fork-join, queue and future operations, and of shutdown hooks.
    FileDispatch
    Dispatch of file operations: reads, writes, opens, closes, maps, transfers, fsync, truncation, deletion and moves.
    HookDemand
    Callback through which the runtime asks the instrumentation layer to weave the hooks for a set of operations before a scenario that needs them starts.
    MethodDispatch
    Dispatch of method entry and exit for the methods a MethodSelector names.
    NetworkDispatch
    Dispatch of socket, socket channel, datagram, selector and TLS operations, with each call's peer and byte count.
    ProcessDispatch
    Dispatch of child process starts and waits.
    RuntimeDispatch
    Dispatch of JVM runtime operations: gc and exit requests, reflection, direct buffers, serialization, class loading and definition, resources, native libraries, zip, JNDI and JMX.
    ThreadDispatch
    Dispatch of thread operations (starts, sleeps, parks, monitor entries, thread-local access) and of the session hand-off between threads.
